final_findings.message: The new implementation uses `types.map` which only works on true Array instances. The original code iterated over any array‑like object via its `length` property, so callers that pass an array‑like (e.g., arguments or a custom object with numeric keys) will now cause a TypeError. This changes the function’s contract and can break existing usage.

Using `Array.prototype.map` without verifying that `types` is defined may throw a TypeError when `types` is `null` or `undefined`. The previous loop would also throw on accessing `length`, but the map call masks the original intent of handling an empty array gracefully. Adding an explicit check would preserve original behavior.
